items.title: William "Ba Ba" Ridgley Interview, 1959-06-02
items.q: He played with Manuel Perez a lot.

ctx.x: Did you know him? I was a trombone player, too, wasn't he? Yes, from downtown.
He played with Manuel Perez a lot.
Yeah, yeah. That's right. George Field. He was good.

items.title: William "Ba Ba" Ridgley Interview, 1961-04-07
items.q: Now, Emanuel Perez, is that right? Is it Perez? No. Yeah, he was a cornet player.

ctx.x: Did he play with other bands that you know of?

He played at other bands before he played with me. And he played with Bill and Terry Brass bands and things. He played with them. He played lots of bands in the city. Lots of jobs. He's a fine old man. And he was the one that connected us with Celestine, Frank Wilson. He was playing cornet and he did more plays. And he knew Celestine and he told us in Civil East band about Celestine. We went to see him and we got him. That's how we got together. Now, Emanuel Perez, is that right? Is it Perez? No. Yeah, he was a…
Emanuel Perez was a cornet player. Emanuel was a, I never did he ever play cornet.

items.title: William "Ba Ba" Ridgley Interview, 1961-04-11
items.q: the old man George Moret was at Excelsior, and Manuel Perez was the Onward band.

ctx.x: When did they start playing by head in the street, in parades and funerals?

Well, the, you see, the Excelsior band and the Onward band, those bands from downtown, the old man George Moret was at Excelsior, and Manuel Perez was the Onward band. Well, those fellows always had, uh, reading musicians, see, they had better reading musicians downtown than they did uptown, see? They were real better musicians, plenty of them. And the most of the faking was from uptown, I guess. But that had been going on with them up there a long time. See, they go to Manmoretti and them and they ain't bad man.…
They had to play your voice.
